summary: Umpqua NF lookout site in Douglas County, OR: 30-foot L-4 tower dated 1935, removed or destroyed 1960; sources differ on timing; none describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 cab, 14-by-14, on a 30-foot round timber tower
facts.status_note: Register says removed and destroyed in 1960; firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1950s; firelookout.com and the FFLOS Oregon list say the tower is gone

staffing.status: staffed in 1937: a News-Review item quoted on Rex's page says Joe Chamberlain was then responsible for the lookout station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives removal and destruction in 1960; firelookout.com says the tower was abandoned in the 1950s. The story reports both dates and does not choose between them.

The register and firelookout.com give 1935. A News-Review item of April 17, 1936, quoted on Rex's page, reports a new lookout house on Coyote point was built but gives no year. The story keeps 1935 and notes the 1936 item.

The register gives N 43.004896 W 122.709655; the Oregon list gives 43.00384, -122.70961, about 0.001 degree of latitude apart. The story gives no coordinates, so the difference does not change any sentence.

notes_for_editor: Gone lookout. No source describes the site today, so the story says so and gives no view or remains. Access is not sourced, so the access key is omitted. The 1950s abandonment is decade-only, so it sits in status_note rather than events. The register cites a 1942 photo from the Ron Kemnow collection, and Rex's page credits a 1942 Tiller Ranger District Collection photo, but no image URL was captured, so no photos entry. Brief record checked (built 1935, removed 1960, registered 2019, gone, 30 ft L-4, USFS). Fact-check 2026-10-09 corrected the Chamberlain tense, reworded the timing conflict, and added evidence for the named staffer and the News-Review attribution.
